mu_name_from: MuMain's ZzzOpenData.cpp loads the group as MODEL_SWORD + i from Sword{i+1}, so Sword03.bmd is index 2, which OpenMU's 0.75 table names the Rapier. MuWeapons.cs agrees from the client's side: `new("Rapier", "Sword03.bmd", WeaponStance.Sword, ...)`.
why_this_one: Hanzo's counter is the last shop in Lorencia with lines that do not resolve, and this is one of them. A shelf drops what it cannot draw - shared/Market builds the row and leaves out anything whose group and number find no asset - so the blacksmith sold ten of his twenty-four lines and the rest of the counter was empty air. The Rapier is his slot 51 at +2, and the second-cheapest blade he sells - fifty strength and forty agility, which is the only low sword that asks for both.

stats.note: The item's own row, copied from OpenMU's 0.75 initialiser rather than restated, with the call it came from beside it.
stats.from: openmu/src/Persistence/Initialization/Version075/Items/Weapons.cs. The 0.75 table, which is the version this server is being built to.
stats.call_note: CreateWeapon(group, number, slot, skillNumber, width, height, dropsFromMonsters, name, dropLevel, minimumDamage, maximumDamage, attackSpeed, durability, magicPower, levelRequirement, strengthRequirement, agilityRequirement, energyRequirement, vitalityRequirement, wizardClass, knightClass, elfClass).
stats.width_note: Width is where OpenMU keeps two-handedness - `if (group < Bows && width == 2)` - and one here agrees with MuWeapons.cs's TwoHanded: false. It is also what takes a fifth off the price: shared/Market.Coin reads the footprint's width to tell a one-handed weapon from a two-handed one.
stats.classes_from: The last three ints of the call are the wizard, knight and elf flags, and MuWeapons.cs carries the same set from the client's side.

stance_from: MuWeapons.cs: WeaponStance.Sword, TwoHanded: false. Actions 4 and 17, the family the Kris, the Short Sword and the Hand Axe already walk in. A one-handed blade leaves the shield hand free, which is the whole point of it on a counter that is mostly shields.
sheet_from: Data/Item/sword04.OZJ (32x32), from MuMain. The .bmd names sword04.jpg; 49 triangles, one mesh. The sheet is numbered one past the model, which is MU's habit across the sword group and not a mistake here.
material_note:
Four islands on thirty-two square, which is the whole of what MU shipped for this sword - the smallest sheet any blade in the project stands on after the Morning Star's sixteen.

Island 0 is the blade: nine triangles running Z 16 to 157, sampling the narrow bright strip up the right of the sheet at (131, 129, 125) and chroma 9. Achromatic and bright, so blade steel, and the one island here where the mill's grain running along the length is the right thing to draw.

Islands 2 and 3 are the swept hilt - the ornate basket that fills most of the sheet - at (167, 161, 150) chroma 18 and (178, 173, 164) chroma 14. Achromatic too, so not the Short Sword's brass, and plate_steel rather than steel for the reason the shields record: a basket's islands run every way at once and a grain that is long in V smears across them. Cast pitting looks the same whichever way the island faces.

Island 1 is the grip, at (84, 77, 59) chroma 28 - the dark banded block along the bottom of the sheet with the gold pommel cap at its end. leather_wrap: the bands are the winding, and they are the subject rather than a stripe laid over it.
open_question: Island 1's ten triangles cover the wound grip and the gold pommel cap together, and the cap is a cast fitting where the grip is not. The island is the unit of assignment and it is also the limit; the wrap is most of it, so the wrap wins.
